name: Cassandra Core Suite
description: Comprehensive evaluation cases for reasoning, context, and security.

cases.name: Simple Bug Fix
cases.description: Tests if the agent can find a simple logic bug in a Go function.
cases.rubric: The agent should identify that the `Divide` function does not check for division by zero.

cases.name: Interface Contract Violation
cases.description: Tests if the agent gathers cross-file context to identify signature/contract mismatches.
cases.rubric: The agent MUST identify that `CreateAndSave` in `service.go` passes a potentially nil user to `SaveUser`, which explicitly requires a non-nil pointer in `repository.go`.

cases.name: Security: Path Traversal
cases.description: Tests if the agent identifies logical security vulnerabilities in file-serving code.
cases.rubric: The agent MUST identify the path traversal vulnerability in the `/file` handler and recommend using `filepath.Clean` or a boundary check.

cases.name: Local Agents Convention
cases.description: Tests if the agent discovers and adheres to local directory-specific instructions (AGENTS.md).
cases.rubric: The agent MUST identify that the new code uses raw `db.Query` instead of the mandated `SafeQuery` wrapper defined in `internal/db/AGENTS.md`.

cases.name: Unupdated Caller Blast Radius
cases.description: Tests if the agent searches for existing callers across the repository when a function's return unit or semantics change.
cases.rubric: The agent MUST search the repository for callers of `ParseTimeout`, identify that untouched callers (`pkg/client/http.go` and/or `cmd/worker/worker.go`) still multiply the return value by `time.Second` after `ParseTimeout` was changed to return milliseconds (causing timeouts to be 1000x too long), and reject the change.

cases.name: Clean PR False-Positive Restraint
cases.description: Tests if the agent approves a well-implemented, well-tested change without inventing false-positive blocking issues.
cases.rubric: The agent MUST approve the change (`Approve`) and MUST NOT raise false-positive blocking issues (such as falsely claiming `onEvict` is called unsafely outside the mutex lock, which is explicitly mandated by `internal/cache/REVIEWERS.md` to prevent deadlocks).

cases.name: Concurrency: Goroutine Leak on Context Cancellation
cases.description: Tests if the agent identifies a goroutine leak when a select statement abandons an unbuffered channel upon context cancellation.
cases.rubric: The agent MUST identify the goroutine leak in `Service.Get`: when `ctx.Done()` fires before `FetchRecord` completes, `Get` returns early and the spawned goroutine blocks indefinitely trying to send to the unbuffered `resCh` channel. The agent should recommend using a buffered channel (`make(chan fetchResult, 1)`) or propagating `ctx`.
